chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-'Alawi, from al-'Umarki al-Nawfali, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a people who performed salat in congregation on a ship: where should the Imam stand? And if there are women with them, what should they do? Should they pray standing or sitting? He said: They should pray standing, and if they are not able to stand, they should pray sitting. The Imam stands in front of them, and the women are behind them. If the ship tosses, the women sit and the men pray, and there is no harm in the women being alongside them.

key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: the women participating in the prayer
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.بِحِيَالِهِمْ: alongside them or opposite their position
key_terms.سَفِينَةٍ: a ship or vessel at sea

ai.seo_question: How should congregational salat be performed on a ship, and where should the Imam and women stand?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for performing congregational salat on a ship. It explains the default arrangement of the Imam, men, and women, and allows sitting when standing is not possible due to inability or instability.
